fresh_internal_checks.check: The general trace lemma concerns closed positive (1,1)-currents carried coefficientwise by a common Borel Lebesgue null set, in every positive dimension.
It uses one arbitrary smooth Hermitian trace form, not a Gauduchon equation or top-degree mass bound.
The exact local-potential statement and preceding argument in Demailly Chapter III, Proposition 1.19, page 135 are read at their cited scope.
Local positive-current potentials can be scaled to the book ddc normalization; no numerical coefficient from a different normalization is imported.
The difference of local potentials is locally integrable and its distributional Hessian is the difference of the currents.
Dividing the equal-trace equation by the positive smooth Hermitian volume gives a scalar second-order operator with inverse-Hermitian positive principal matrix.
Uniform ellipticity is used on smaller compactly contained balls; no global inverse equation or mass hypothesis is needed.
Classical distributional elliptic regularity makes the potential difference smooth.
Its Hessian is smooth and carried by the common null set, forcing every coefficient to vanish.
The argument is local and proves equality globally without comparing current cohomology classes.
The actual source-book pages 138-140 are completely read, including the complete-pluripolar definition, cutoff construction, extension proof and restriction corollary.
Demailly Theorem 2.3 and Corollary 2.4 explicitly require a closed complete pluripolar set; that condition is retained in the new model application.
Closed pole sets pull back to closed sets, and smooth local psh correction shows local complete pluripolarity.
The corrected Hessian is closed and positive on the whole local ball and has locally finite coefficient mass, so the restriction corollary applies.
The nonclosed smooth background is not treated as a closed current; its difference from the correcting Hessian has no mass on the pole set.
The restricted corrected Hessians therefore equal the actual polar curvature restrictions, and glue as closed positive currents.
The union of the two pole sets is a Borel Lebesgue null carrier for both currents.
Equality of the fixed Gauduchon trace measures invokes the foundation lemma; equality of currents gives the converse directly.
Strict positivity of all fixed denominators makes zero supremum comparison equivalent to zero difference in every trace coordinate.
The recovery statement covers closed-pole genuine potentials and does not assert separation of every ordinary model from the resulting current data.
No current-recovery statement is asserted here for arbitrary nonclosed pole sets or merely pluripolar subsets without the complete-pole hypotheses.
No quantitative inverse trace estimate, current-limit realization, complete general model topology or new formal problem closure is claimed.
